paragraphs: CVB Financial Corp. (referred to herein on an unconsolidated basis as "CVB" and on a consolidated basis as "we", "our" or the "Company") is a bank holding company incorporated in California on April 27, 1981 and registered with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System ("Federal Reserve") under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the "BHCA"). The Company commenced business on December 30, 1981 when, pursuant to a reorganization, it acquired all of the voting stock of Chino Valley Bank. On March 29, 1996, Chino Valley Bank changed its name to Citizens Business Bank, and on December 15, 2025, Citizens Business Bank changed its name to Citizens Business Bank, National Association ("CBB" or the "Bank"). The Bank is our principal asset. The Company has one inactive subsidiary, Chino Valley Bancorp.

CVB's principal business is to serve as a holding company for the Bank and for other banking or banking related subsidiaries, which the Company may establish or acquire. CVB has not engaged in any other material activities to date. As a legal entity separate and distinct from its subsidiaries, CVB's principal source of funds is, and will continue to be, dividends paid by and other funds advanced from the Bank and capital raised directly by CVB. Legal limitations are imposed on the amount of dividends that may be paid and loans that may be made by the Bank to CVB. See "Item 1. Business — Regulation and Supervision — Dividends." As of December 31, 2025, the Company had $15.63 billion in total consolidated assets, $8.62 billion in net loans, $12.07 billion in deposits, and $2.30 billion in shareholders' equity.
The principal executive offices of CVB and the Bank are located at 701 North Haven Avenue, Suite 350, Ontario, California. Our phone number is (909) 980-4030.

The Bank commenced operations on August 9, 1974. Effective December 15, 2025, the Bank converted from a California-chartered bank to a national banking association chartered under the laws of the United States. The Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System and of the Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco ("FHLB"), which is a member bank of the Federal Home Loan Bank System. The Bank's deposit accounts are insured under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act up to maximum amount currently allowable under federal law. The Bank is currently subject to the examination and regulation by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (the "OCC") and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC").
At December 31, 2025, the Bank had $15.63 billion in assets, $8.62 billion in net loans, $12.13 billion in deposits, and $2.27 billion in total equity.

As of December 31, 2025, the Bank had 62 Banking Centers ("Centers") and one loan production office located throughout California. We also have three trust offices located in Ontario, Newport Beach, and Pasadena. These offices serve as sales offices for the Bank's wealth management, trust and investment products.

The Bank's goal is to be the premier financial services company operating throughout the state of California, servicing the comprehensive financial needs of successful small-and medium-sized businesses and their owners. Through our network of Centers, we emphasize personalized service combined with a wide array of banking and trust services for businesses, professionals and individuals located in the service areas of our Centers. Although we focus the marketing of our services to small-and medium-sized businesses, a wide range of banking, investment and trust services are made available to the markets we serve.

We offer a wide range of bank deposit instruments. These include checking, savings, money market and certificates of time deposit for both business and personal accounts, municipalities and districts, and specialized deposit products for title and escrow. We also serve as a federal tax depository for our business customers.

We provide a full complement of lending products, including commercial, agribusiness, consumer, SBA, real estate, and construction loans, as well as equipment and vehicle leasing. Commercial products include lines of credit and other working capital financing, accounts receivable lending and letters of credit. Agribusiness products are loans to finance the operating needs of wholesale dairy farm operations, cattle feeders, livestock raisers, and farmers. We provide bank qualified lease financing for municipal governments. Commercial real estate and construction loans are secured by a range of property types and include both owner-occupied and investor owned properties. We also offer borrowers the ability to enter into interest rate swaps. Financing products for consumers include automobile leasing and financing, lines of credit, credit cards, home mortgages, and home equity loans and lines of credit.

We also offer a wide range of specialized services designed for the needs of our commercial customers. These services include treasury management systems for monitoring and managing cash flow, a merchant card processing program, armored pick-up and delivery, payroll services, remote deposit capture, electronic funds transfers, domestic and international wires and automated clearinghouse, on-line account access, and international business activities including foreign exchange and letters of credit for international trade. We make available investment products offered by other providers to our customers, including mutual funds, a full array of fixed income vehicles and a program to diversify our customers' funds in federally insured time certificates of deposit of other institutions.

In addition, we offer a wide range of financial services and trust services through our CitizensTrust division. These services include fiduciary services, mutual funds, annuities, 401(k) plans and individual investment accounts.

On December 17, 2025, the Company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") with Heritage Commerce Corp. In accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, Heritage will merge with and into the Company in an all-stock transaction, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation. Promptly following the Merger, Heritage Bank of Commerce, a California banking corporation and wholly-owned subsidiary of Heritage will merge with and into CBB, with CBB continuing as the surviving bank (the "Bank Merger").

Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, Heritage shareholders will receive 0.65 shares of the Company's common stock for each share of Heritage common stock they own. Upon closing, CVB shareholders will own approximately 77% and Heritage shareholders will own approximately 23% of the combined company. The combined company will have approximately $22 billion in assets, more than 80 centers and offices, and a deeply rooted presence in the State of California's key economic centers. The acquisition is presently expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of regulatory approvals, Heritage and CVB shareholder approvals, and other customary closing conditions.
We are a community bank with one reportable operating segment. See Note 3 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies — Business Segments of the notes to the consolidated financial statements.

paragraphs: In the course of conducting our business operations, we are exposed to a variety of risks. Some of these risks are inherent in the financial services industry and others are more specific to our own business. Together with the other information on the risks we face and our management of risk contained in this Annual Report, the following presents the most significant risks of which we are currently aware that may affect us. Events or circumstances arising from one or more of these risks could adversely affect our business, financial condition, operating results and prospects and the value and price of our common stock could decline. The risks identified below are not intended to be a comprehensive list of all risks we face, and additional risks that we may currently view as not material may also impair our business operations, financial condition and operating results.
• Our allowance for credit losses may not be sufficient to cover actual losses.
• We may be required to make additional provisions for credit losses and charge-off additional loans in the future, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
• Our dairy & livestock and agribusiness lending presents unique credit risks.
• Our loan portfolio is predominantly secured by real estate in California and thus we have a higher degree of credit risk from a downturn in our real estate markets.
• Our commercial real estate loan portfolio exposes us to risks that may be greater than the risks related to our other loans.

paragraphs: The following discussion provides information about the results of operations, financial condition, liquidity, and capital resources of CVB Financial Corp. and its wholly owned subsidiary. This information is intended to facilitate the understanding and assessment of significant changes and trends related to our financial condition and the results of our operations. This discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and the audited consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes presented elsewhere in this report.

The preparation of these consolidated financial statements requires management to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of our financial statements. Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions.

Critical accounting policies are defined as those that are reflective of significant judgments and uncertainties, and are essential to understanding Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations. The following is a summary of the more judgmental and complex accounting estimates and principles. In each area, we have identified the variables most important in the estimation process. We have used the best information available to make the necessary estimates to value the related assets and liabilities. Actual performance that differs from our estimates and future changes in the key variables could change future valuations and impact the results of operations.

Allowance for Credit Losses ("ACL") — Our allowance for credit losses is based upon lifetime loss rate models developed from an estimation framework that uses historical lifetime loss experiences to derive loss rates at a collective pool level. We measure the expected credit losses on a collective (pooled) basis for those loans that share similar risk characteristics. We have three collective loan pools: Commercial Real Estate, Commercial and Industrial, and Consumer. Our ACL amounts are largely driven by portfolio characteristics, including loss history and various risk attributes, and the economic outlook for certain macroeconomic variables. Risk attributes for commercial real estate loans include original loan to value ratios, origination year, loan seasoning, and macroeconomic variables that include GDP growth, commercial real estate price index and unemployment rate. Risk attributes for commercial and industrial loans include internal risk ratings, borrower industry sector, loan credit spreads and macroeconomic variables that include unemployment rate and BBB spread. The macroeconomic variables for Consumer include unemployment rate and GDP. The Commercial Real Estate methodology is applied over commercial real estate loans, a portion of construction loans, and a portion of SBA loans. The Commercial and Industrial methodology is applied over a substantial portion of the Company's commercial and industrial loans, all dairy & livestock and agribusiness loans, municipal lease receivables, as well as the remaining portion of SBA loans. The Consumer methodology is applied to SFR mortgage loans, consumer loans, as well as the remaining construction loans. In addition to determining the quantitative life of loan loss rate to be applied against the amortized cost basis of the portfolio segments, management reviews current conditions and forecasts to determine whether adjustments are needed to ensure that the life of loan loss rates reflect both the current state of the portfolio, and expectations for macroeconomic changes. Our methodology for assessing the appropriateness of the allowance is reviewed on a regular basis and considers overall risks in the Bank's loan portfolio.

For a full discussion of our methodology of assessing the adequacy of the allowance for credit losses, see "Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operation — Risk Management" and Note 3 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Note 5 — Loans and Lease Finance Receivables and Allowance for Credit Losses of our consolidated financial statements presented elsewhere in this report.

Business Combinations — The Company applies the acquisition method of accounting for business combinations. Under the acquisition method, the acquiring entity in a business combination recognizes the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their acquisition date fair values. Management utilizes prevailing valuation techniques appropriate for the asset or liability being measured in determining these fair values. These fair values are estimates and are subject to adjustment for up to one year after the acquisition date or when additional information relative to the closing date fair values becomes available and such information is considered final, whichever is earlier. Any excess of the purchase price over amounts allocated to assets acquired, including identifiable intangible assets, and liabilities assumed is recorded as goodwill. Where amounts
allocated to assets acquired and liabilities assumed is greater than the purchase price, a bargain purchase gain would be recognized. Acquisition related costs are expensed as incurred.

Valuation and Recoverability of Goodwill — Goodwill represented $765.8 million of our $15.63 billion in total assets as of December 31, 2025. The Company has one reportable segment. Goodwill has an indefinite useful life and is not amortized, but is tested for impairment at least annually, or more frequently, if events and circumstances exist that indicate that a goodwill impairment test should be performed. Such events and circumstances may include among others, a significant adverse change in legal factors or in the general business climate, significant decline in our stock price and market capitalization, unanticipated competition, the testing for recoverability of a significant asset group within the reporting unit, and an adverse action or assessment by a regulating body. Any adverse change in these factors could have a significant impact on the recoverability of goodwill and could have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.

Based on the results of our annual goodwill impairment test, we determined that no goodwill impairment charges were required as our single reportable segment's estimated fair value exceeded its carrying amount. See Note 6 — Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets of our consolidated financial statements presented elsewhere in this report.

For a complete discussion and disclosure of other accounting policies see Note 3 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies of the Company's consolidated financial statements presented elsewhere in this report.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we reported net earnings of $209.3 million, compared with $200.7 million for 2024, a $8.6 million, or 4.28%, increase from the prior year. Diluted earnings per share of $1.52 for 2025, increased by $0.08, or 5.61%, when compared to $1.44 for 2024. Market interest rates stayed elevated throughout the first eight months of 2024 until the Federal Reserve initiated a series of rate cuts in September 2024. This shift in the interest rate environment materially affected the Company's net interest income and overall earnings during 2025. Net earnings benefited from higher net interest income, driven primarily by the expansion in net interest margin. The improvement reflected a reduction in overall cost of funds, particularly on borrowings, as a result of the Company's balance sheet deleveraging efforts in late 2024. Net earnings of $209.3 million produced a return on average equity ("ROAE") of 9.26%, a return on average tangible common equity ("ROATCE") of 14.28% and a return on average assets ("ROAA") of 1.36%. Our net interest margin, tax equivalent ("NIM"), was 3.36% for 2025, while our efficiency ratio was 46.0%.

Net interest income of $460.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, increased $12.9 million, or 2.89%, compared to the same period of 2024. Interest income decreased by $36.8 million, or 5.84%, in 2025, while interest expense decreased $49.8 million year-over-year. Cost of funds for 2025 decreased by 29 basis points over 2024, while the earning asset yield decreased by two basis points. Average earning assets declined by $798.3 million year-over-year.

Noninterest income of $55.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, increased by $0.7 million, or 1.28%, compared to the same period of 2024. Trust and investment income for 2025 grew by $1.3 million, or 9.50%, from the prior year. Noninterest income in 2025 included a $11.0 million in losses on the sale of AFS investment securities, a $6.0 million legal settlement, and a $2.3 million gain in OREO, while 2024 included a total pre-tax loss of $28.3 million from the sale of $467 million of AFS securities partially offset by a pre-tax gain of $25.9 million from the sale-leaseback of four buildings.

Noninterest expense increased from $233.6 million in 2024 to $237.3 million in 2025. The $3.7 million increase in noninterest expense was primarily driven by higher software related costs associated with the continued investments in technology and infrastructure. In addition, noninterest expense included $1.6 million of acquisition related costs to the announced merger with Heritage.

paragraphs: CVB Financial Corp.（於本文件中未合併會計時稱為 "CVB"，於合併會計時稱為 "we"、"our" 或 the "Company"）為一間在加州註冊的銀行控股公司，於1981年4月27日成立，並已根據1956年銀行控股公司法案（"BHCA"）經修正後的條文，向聯邦儲備銀行（"Federal Reserve"）註冊。本公司於1981年12月30日開始營業，當時根據一項重組，取得Chino Valley Bank全部投票權股票。1996年3月29日，Chino Valley Bank更名為Citizens Business Bank，並於2025年12月15日，Citizens Business Bank更名為Citizens Business Bank, National Association（"CBB" 或 the "Bank"）。該銀行為本公司主要資產。本公司有一間無營運子公司，為Chino Valley Bancorp。

CVB的主要業務為擔任銀行及其相關銀行子公司的控股公司，本公司可能設立或取得之其他銀行或銀行相關子公司。CVB至今未從事任何其他重大業務活動。作為與其子公司分開且獨立的法律實體，CVB的主要資金來源為，並持續為銀行所支付的股息及其他由銀行提供的資金，以及CVB直接籌集的資本。法律限制了銀行對CVB所能支付的股息及貸款金額。請參閱 "Item 1. Business — Regulation and Supervision — Dividends." 截至2025年12月31日，本公司總合併資產為15.63十億美元，淨貸款為8.62十億美元，存款為12.07十億美元，以及股東權益為2.30十億美元。
CVB及銀行的主要營業處所位於加州 Ontario 的701 North Haven Avenue, Suite 350。本公司電話為（909）980-4030。

銀行於1974年8月9日開始營運。自2025年12月15日起，銀行已從加州發照的銀行轉為根據美國法律設立的國家銀行協會（"CBB" 或 the "Bank"）。銀行為聯邦儲備系統成員，並為舊金山聯邦住宅貸款銀行（"FHLB"）成員，而FHLB為聯邦住宅貸款銀行系統的成員銀行。銀行的存款賬戶根據《聯邦存款保險法》投保，最高投保額為現行聯邦法律所允許的上限。銀行目前受美國國庫局（"OCC"）及聯邦存款保險公司（"FDIC"）的監督與管理。
截至2025年12月31日，銀行資產為15.63十億美元，淨貸款為8.62十億美元，存款為12.13十億美元，以及總權益為2.27十億美元。
截至2025年12月31日，銀行擁有62間銀行中心（"Centers"）及一間貸款業務辦公室，位於加州各地。我們亦在Ontario、Newport Beach及Pasadena設有三間信託辦公室。這些辦公室作為銀行財富管理、信託及投資產品的銷售據點。
銀行的目標為成為在加州運作的首選金融服務公司，服務成功的小型及中型企業及其所有者。透過我們的銀行中心網路，我們強調個人化服務，並提供廣泛的銀行及信託服務，以服務位於我們銀行中心服務範圍內的企業、專業人士及個人。雖然我們將服務行銷重點放在小型及中型企業，但我們為所服務的市場提供廣泛的銀行、投資及信託服務。
我們提供廣泛的銀行存款產品。這些產品包括企業及個人帳戶、地方政府及區議會的支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶、貨幣市場帳戶及定期存款證書，以及專門為地產及過戶業務設計的存款產品。我們亦為企業客戶提供聯邦稅收存放處服務。

本公司提供完整的貸款產品組合，包括商業貸款、農業貸款、消費者貸款、SBA貸款、不動產貸款、建設貸款，以及設備與車輛租賃。商業貸款產品包括信用線與其他營運資金融資、應收帳款貸款與信用證。農業貸款產品為用以資金融通 Wholesale dairy 奶農場營運需求、牛飼養者、畜牧場經營者與農民的貸款。本公司提供符合銀行標準的租賃融資服務給地方政府。商業不動產與建設貸款以多種不動產類型為擔保，包括自用與投資者所有的不動產。本公司亦提供借款人進行利率交換的選擇。消費者融資產品包括汽車租賃與貸款、信用線、信用卡、住宅房貸與住宅貸款及信用線。

本公司亦提供廣泛的專業化服務，以符合商業客戶的需要。這些服務包括用以監控與管理現金流的財務管理系統、商家卡處理方案、裝甲車提款與配送、薪資服務、遠端存款捕獲、電子資金轉帳、國內與國際電匯及自動清算系統、線上帳戶存取，以及國際業務活動，包括外匯與國際貿易用信用證。本公司亦為客戶提供其他機構所提供的投資產品，包括共同基金、完整的固定收益投資工具，以及一個用以分散客戶資金的計畫，該計畫涉及其他機構發行的 federally insured 時期存款證。
此外，本公司透過 CitizensTrust 分部提供廣泛的金融服務與信託服務。這些服務包括信託服務、共同基金、年金、401(k) 計畫與個人投資帳戶。

2025 年 12 月 17 日，本公司與 Heritage Commerce Corp 簽訂了合併協議（"合併協議"）。根據合併協議的條款與條件，Heritage 將與本公司合併，以全股票交易方式進行，本公司將作為存續公司。合併後，Heritage Bank of Commerce，一家位於加州的銀行公司且為 Heritage 的 wholly-owned 子公司，將與 CBB 合併，CBB 將作為存續銀行（"銀行合併"）。

{"Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, Heritage shareholders will receive 0.65 shares of the Company's common stock for each share of Heritage common stock they own.": '依合併協議條款，Heritage股東將就其持有的每一股Heritage普通股，取得本公司0.65股普通股。', 'Upon closing, CVB shareholders will own approximately 77% and Heritage shareholders will own approximately 23% of the combined company.': '合併完成後，CVB股東將持有約77%、Heritage股東將持有約23%的合併後公司股份。', "The combined company will have approximately $22 billion in assets, more than 80 centers and offices, and a deeply rooted presence in the State of California's key economic centers.": '合併後公司將擁有約22十億美元資產、超過80個中心及辦公室，並在加州的關鍵經濟中心有深厚根基。', 'The acquisition is presently expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, subject to satisfaction of regulatory approvals, Heritage and CVB shareholder approvals, and other customary closing conditions.': '此併購案預計於2026年第二季完成，但需符合監管機構批准、Heritage及CVB股東同意，及其他慣例性交割條件。'}

paragraphs: 以下討論提供有關 CVB Financial Corp. 及其 wholly owned subsidiary 的營運成果、財務狀況、流動性及資本資源之資訊。此資訊旨在協助瞭解與評估與我們財務狀況及營運成果相關的重大變動與趨勢。此討論與分析應與本年度 Form 10-K 年度報告，以及本報告其他地方所載之經審計合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。
這些合併財務報表之編製，需管理階層做出估計與判斷，影響所報告之資產與負債、收入與費用，以及相關或有資產與負債之揭露。實際結果可能因不同假設或條件而與這些估計不同。
關鍵會計政策被定義為反映重大判斷與不確定性，且對瞭解管理階層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析至關重要。以下為會計估計與原則中較具判斷性與複雜性的總結。在每個領域，我們已識別出估計過程中最為重要的變數。我們已使用可得的最佳資訊，以做出必要的估計，以評估相關資產與負債之價值。實際表現若與我們之估計不同，或關鍵變數未來有所改變，可能會改變未來之評估，並影響營運成果。

貸款信用減損準備（"ACL"）—— 我們之貸款信用減損準備係根據從歷史貸款損失經驗中推導出之貸款損失率模型，於集體池層級建立。我們針對具有相似風險特徵之貸款，以集體（集體池）方式衡量預期信用損失。我們有三個集體貸款池：商業不動產、商業及工業、以及消費貸款。我們之 ACL 金額主要受資產組合特性影響，包括損失歷史與各種風險屬性，以及特定總體經濟變數之經濟展望。商業不動產貸款之風險屬性包括原始貸款對價值比率、貸款發行年份、貸款年資，以及總體經濟變數，包括 GDP 成長率、商業不動產價格指數與失業率。商業及工業貸款之風險屬性包括內部風險評級、借款人產業部門、貸款信用 spreads，以及總體經濟變數，包括失業率與 BBB spreads。消費貸款之總體經濟變數包括失業率與 GDP。商業不動產之方法論適用於商業不動產貸款、部分建設貸款，以及部分 SBA 貸款。商業及工業之方法論適用於本公司大部分商業及工業貸款、所有乳製品與畜牧業及農業企業貸款、市政租賃應收款，以及剩餘部分之 SBA 貸款。消費貸款之方法論適用於單戶住宅抵押貸款、消費貸款，以及剩餘建設貸款。除了確定應適用於資產組合段落之帳面價值之貸款損失率外，管理階層也會審視當前情況與預測，以判斷是否需要調整，以確保貸款損失率反映資產組合目前狀態及對總體經濟變動之預期。我們評估貸款信用減損準備是否適當之方法論會定期審查，並考量銀行貸款組合整體之風險。
有關本公司評估信用減損準備金是否足夠之方法論之完整討論，請參閱「第 7 項，管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析與評論 — 風險管理」及本公司合併財務報表中其他處所載明之「第 3 項 — 重要會計政策摘要」及「第 5 項 — 應收貸款及租賃融資款與信用減損準備金」。

企業併購 — 本公司採用收購法則會計處理企業併購。根據收購法則，於企業併購中，取得企業之取得方應以其取得日之公允價值計入取得之資產與承擔之負債。管理階層會根據所測量之資產或負債之性質，使用適當之估值技術以確定這些公允價值。這些公允價值為估計值，並可能在取得日後最多一年內，或當有關取得日公允價值之額外資訊變得可用且被認為為最終資訊時，進行調整，以較早者為準。任何購買價格超過分配至取得之資產（包括可辨認無形資產）及承擔之負債之金額之差額，應計入商譽。於
分配至取得之資產及承擔之負債之金額高於購買價格時，應認列 bargain purchase gain。與企業併購相關之費用應於發生時計入費用。

商譽之價值與可收回性 — 商譽於 2025 年 12 月 31 日本公司總資產 15.63 十億美元中佔有 765.8 百萬美元。本公司有一個應報告分部。商譽具有無限使用壽命，不進行攤銷，但至少每年進行一次減損測試，若存在事件或情況顯示應進行商譽減損測試，則更頻繁進行測試。這些事件或情況可能包括但不限於：法律因素或一般營商環境的重大不利變動、本公司股票價格與市價資本大幅下跌、未預期之競爭、報告單位內重大資產組合之可收回性測試，以及監管機構之不利行動或評估。任何這些因素之不利變動都可能對商譽之可收回性產生重大影響，並可能對本公司合併財務報表產生重大影響。
根據我們年度商譽減損測試的結果，我們認定無需提列商譽減損費用，因本公司單一應報告分部的預估公平價值超過其帳面價值。請參閱本報告其他處所列之本公司合併財務報表之附註 6 — 商譽及其他無形資產。
有關其他會計政策的完整討論與揭露，請參閱本報告其他處所列之本公司合併財務報表之附註 3 — 重要會計政策摘要。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度，我們報告淨收益為 209.3 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 200.7 百萬美元增加 8.6 百萬美元，或 4.28%。2025 年的每股稀釋收益為 1.52 美元，較 2024 年的 1.44 美元增加 0.08 美元，或 5.61%。2024 年前八個月市場利率持續偏高，直至 2024 年 9 月聯邦儲備委員會開始進行一系列利率調降。此利率環境的變化對本公司 2025 年的淨利息收入及整體收益產生重大影響。淨收益受益於較高的淨利息收入，主要由淨利息邊際擴張所驅動。此改善反映總體資金成本的降低，特別是在借款方面的降低，這是因為本公司在 2024 年末進行了資產負債表去槓桿化努力的結果。209.3 百萬美元的淨收益產生平均權益回報率（"ROAE"）為 9.26%，平均實質普通權益回報率（"ROATCE"）為 14.28%，以及平均資產回報率（"ROAA"）為 1.36%。我們 2025 年的淨利息邊際（"NIM"）為 3.36%，而我們的效率比率為 46.0%。
2025 年截至 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度，淨利息收入為 460.3 百萬美元，較 2024 年同期增加 12.9 百萬美元，或 2.89%。2025 年利息收入減少 36.8 百萬美元，或 5.84%，而利息支出減少 49.8 百萬美元。2025 年的資金成本較 2024 年減少 29 基點，而獲利資產收益率減少 2 基點。平均獲利資產較 2024 年減少 798.3 百萬美元。

2025 年截至 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度，非利息收入為 55.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年同期增加 0.7 百萬美元，或 1.28%。2025 年的信託與投資收入較前一年增加 1.3 百萬美元，或 9.50%。2025 年的非利息收入包括出售 AFS 投資證券產生 11.0 百萬美元的損失、法律和解金 6.0 百萬美元，以及 OREO 產生 2.3 百萬美元的收益，而 2024 年則包括出售 467 百萬美元 AFS 投資證券產生總計 28.3 百萬美元的稅前損失，部分抵銷的是出售四棟大樓的租賃回購產生 25.9 百萬美元的稅前收益。
非利息支出從 2024 年的 233.6 百萬美元增至 2025 年的 237.3 百萬美元。非利息支出增加 3.7 百萬美元，主要是因持續投資於資訊科技與基礎建設所導致的軟體相關成本增加。此外，非利息支出包括 1.6 百萬美元的併購相關費用，用以公告與 Heritage 進行合併。

本公司依賴關鍵人員，若失去其中一位或多位關鍵人員，可能對本公司前景造成重大且不利的影響。
若本公司企業風險管理架構未能有效降低風險及損失，本公司可能遭遇未預期之損失，且營運成果可能受到重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 在進行業務運作的過程中，我們面臨多種風險。其中一些風險是金融服務業內在的，而其他則更特定於我們的業務。與本年度報告中關於我們所面臨的風險及其他風險管理資訊一同參考，以下內容說明了我們目前所知的最重大風險，這些風險可能影響我們。來自這些風險之一或多個的事件或情況可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及前景產生不利影響，並可能導致我們普通股的價值與價格下跌。以下所識別的風險並非我們所面臨風險的完整清單，我們目前可能認為不具重大性的其他風險也可能影響我們的業務運作、財務狀況及營運結果。
• 我們的信用減損準備金可能不足以覆蓋實際的損失。
• 我們可能需要在未來增加信用減損準備金並核銷更多貸款，這可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
• 我們的乳製品及畜牧業貸款業務面臨獨特的信用風險。
• 我們的貸款組合主要以加利福尼亞州的不動產為擔保，因此我們在不動產市場走弱時面臨較高的信用風險。
• 我們的商業不動產貸款組合使我們面臨的風險可能高於與我們其他貸款相關的風險。
